themes_detail.label: Tree damage surge
themes_detail.summary: Damaged tree complaints spiked to 14 THIS WEEK, up 460% from the 2.5-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.67), suggesting a discrete weather event or infrastructure failure affecting Park Slope's canopy.
evidence: 14 damaged tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.5-per-week average over prior 8 weeks (460% spike, z-score 7.67)
Damaged trees rank 9th in 90-day complaint volume at 307 total, but THIS WEEK's surge represents statistical anomaly
Aligns with community board repeated requests to 'Reconstruct or upgrade a park or amenity' and 'Damaged Tree' as emerging infrastructure concern
reporting_angles: Was there a storm or high winds this week that prompted the spike? Interview Parks Dept on response time and tree assessment protocols.
Investigate whether aging street trees in Park Slope are under-maintained; cross-reference with Parks maintenance schedules and pruning records.

themes_detail.label: Rodent infestation acceleration
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints jumped 206% LAST WEEK to 13 complaints versus a 4.2-per-week baseline (z-score: 9.04), signaling a potential pest control emergency or sanitation breakdown in the neighborhood.
evidence: 13 rodent complaints LAST WEEK vs. 4.2-per-week average (206% spike, z-score 9.04—highest severity)
This is one of the sharpest single-category spikes in the dataset, suggesting rapid deterioration rather than gradual trend
Parallels 'Dirty Condition' complaints also up 229% LAST WEEK (60 vs. 18.2 avg), indicating possible sanitation crisis
reporting_angles: Interview residents in affected blocks to locate epicenter; map complaints geographically to identify whether spike is localized (e.g., near subway, market, dumpster area).
Request NYC Health Dept rodent baiting and inspection records for Park Slope; determine whether city response is keeping pace with complaint volume.

themes_detail.label: Bike rack infrastructure failure
themes_detail.summary: Bike rack complaints exploded to 4 THIS WEEK from a 0.4-per-week baseline (967% spike, z-score: 7.49), suggesting either a specific installation failure or a broader lack of functional parking infrastructure in this bike-heavy neighborhood.
evidence: 4 bike rack complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4-per-week average (967% spike, z-score 7.49)
Statistically anomalous even for low-volume category; suggests discrete failure (e.g., damaged racks on specific block or park) rather than systemic issue
Park Slope has high cycling mode share; bike infrastructure gaps are a known community concern
reporting_angles: Locate the 4 THIS WEEK complaints geographically; visit those locations to photograph damaged/missing racks and interview cyclists.
Interview Parks Dept on bike rack maintenance schedule; determine response time to repair requests.

themes_detail.label: Derelict vehicle accumulation
themes_detail.summary: Derelict vehicle complaints surged to 17 LAST WEEK, up 289% from a 4.4-per-week baseline (z-score: 6.14), indicating either a towing enforcement gap or concentration of abandoned vehicles in the district.
evidence: 17 derelict vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 4.4-per-week average (289% spike, z-score 6.14)
Overlaps with 'Illegal Parking' (top complaint at 3,452 over 90 days), suggesting enforcement and street management challenges
Convergence with 'Obstruction' complaints also up 250% LAST WEEK (7 vs. 2.0 avg) hints at broader street-use disorder
reporting_angles: Map derelict vehicle complaints to identify hotspots (specific blocks or parking areas); visit to photograph and interview residents about impacts.
Contact NYPD and Department of Sanitation to obtain towing logs; determine response time and whether 311 complaints are being acted upon.

themes_detail.label: Dirty conditions and sanitation crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dirty condition complaints jumped 229% LAST WEEK to 60 complaints versus an 18.2-per-week baseline (z-score: 5.88), coupled with spikes in rodent and obstruction complaints, pointing to a neighborhood-wide sanitation breakdown.
evidence: 60 dirty condition complaints LAST WEEK vs. 18.2-per-week average (229% spike, z-score 5.88)
Convergence with rodent spike (206%, z-score 9.04) and dumpster complaints up 357% (8 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.8 avg), suggesting cascading sanitation failure
Obstruction complaints also up 250% LAST WEEK (7 vs. 2.0 avg), consistent with littering and debris accumulation
reporting_angles: Conduct neighborhood walk; photograph and geolocate the dirtiest blocks; interview residents and local business owners on what changed in the past 1–2 weeks.
Request NYC Sanitation collection and street sweeping records for Park Slope; determine whether service cuts or worker absences correlate with spike timing.
